description: Add `text` at the end of a document, or under `heading`: at the end of that heading's own text, before its first subsection when it has any (so under a page's title heading it goes in the page's opening, and the answer says so), else at the end of its section. A `heading` the page lacks is refused with the headings it has; to start a new section, put its heading in `text` and leave `heading` out. It touches nothing else, so prefer it for notes, logs and memory. Changes are PROPOSED, never applied blindly: by default the tool returns `Proposed` and your change waits for the user to accept it — that is SUCCESS, never retry it. They are notified. The owner may instead have set the item to let AI edits apply directly, and then the result says `Applied`; or to be reviewed by a colleague, so someone other than the user accepts it. `revises`: the ids of the CHANGES REQUESTED this proposal answers (from the block your reads open with); until a proposal names them, they keep leading your reads. ONE piece of work is ONE change, reviewed on one card: an ingest of a meeting or an email, or one Save to Stuga of several points. Give `change_title` (a few words naming its source, never a page's title) to your FIRST write for it, and pass the `change_id` the answer returns to EVERY later write for it, on every page and database; `change_summary` says what it does. A new page made inside a change, where AI edits wait for a colleague, stays visible only to the user and those who may approve it until it is approved. When your earlier change to a page is still undecided, a write there for another change waits behind it in a queue (`queued_behind`): that is SUCCESS, never retry it. Images written as ![alt](https://…) or as a data: URI are downloaded and stored with the document, so it never hotlinks; the Markdown title slot is the image's visible caption.

change_id.description: The `change_id` your first write for this piece of work returned: pass it to every later write for it.

change_summary.description: What the change does, in a sentence or two, for whoever approves it; a later write may replace it.

change_title.description: Opens a change for this piece of work and returns its `change_id`: a few words naming its source, as "Customer sync, 2026-10-21".

workspace_id.description: The workspace to act in: a `workspace_id` from `workspaces` action:list, which also says which node it is on.

name: markdown_append
title: Append to a document
